fullName: Apache Pulsar's MultiRolesTokenAuthorizationProvider authorizes a client with all roles listed in a claim of its JSON Web Token (JWT).
normalized: cve 2026 105869 apache pulsar s multirolestokenauthorizationprovider authorizes a client with all roles listed in a claim of its json web token jwt the provider is intended for use with token authentication which verifies the token before authorization the provider did not verify the token itself it parsed the token s claims with the signature removed and trusted that authentication had already checked it when authentication and authorization are enabled with a non empty anonymoususerrole setting some http requests whose credentials fail authentication are not rejected but are handled as requests of the anonymous user role for the broker s http endpoints such as the admin rest api this fallback applies to requests that do not name an authentication method and requires strictauthmethod to be false the default where that setting is available for the websocket api failed credentials can also fall back to the anonymous user role this path does not enforce strictauthmethod the authentication data kept for such a request still contained the request s authorization header multirolestokenauthorizationprovider then read the bearer token from that header without verifying its signature and authorized the request with the roles in the token s role claim as a result in deployments that use multirolestokenauthorizationprovider together with a non empty anonymoususerrole and that permit this fallback an unauthenticated client can send an http request for example to the admin rest api or the websocket api with a forged or unsigned token that lists arbitrary roles and be authorized with those roles the impact can include super user access when the token lists a role configured in superuserroles allowing the client to read and change tenants namespaces topics permissions and broker configuration no valid credentials are required deployments are not affected if they use the default authorization provider pulsarauthorizationprovider or another authorization provider or if anonymoususerrole is not set the default requests that authenticate successfully with a valid token are not affected because the token that multirolestokenauthorizationprovider reads is the token that authentication verified connections that use the pulsar binary protocol are not affected by this issue because the broker does not keep client authentication data for connections that it assigns to the anonymous user role in fixed versions multirolestokenauthorizationprovider obtains roles only from tokens that the configured token authentication provider has verified using its configured keys and validation settings broker http requests that are assigned to the anonymous user role are authorized only as that role and invalid tokens cannot supply additional roles to websocket requests the broker fails to start if multirolestokenauthorizationprovider is configured with authorization enabled but without a token authentication provider this issue affects apache pulsar versions from 2 8 1 before 4 0 14 and from 4 1 0 before 4 2 5 4 0 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 0 14 4 1 x and 4 2 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 2 5 users operating versions prior to those listed above should upgrade to the aforementioned patched versions or newer versions the currently supported apache pulsar release lines are 4 0 x and 5 0 x the supported versions schedule is available at https pulsar apache org contribute release policy users who cannot upgrade immediately can remove the anonymoususerrole setting from the broker and websocket service configurations or restrict network access to the http endpoints of these services to trusted clients

fullName: The Pulsar broker serves two schema commands on its binary protocol: GetSchema, which returns the schema registered for a topic, and GetOrCreateSchema, which registers a new schema version for an existing topic.
normalized: cve 2026 105926 the pulsar broker serves two schema commands on its binary protocol getschema which returns the schema registered for a topic and getorcreateschema which registers a new schema version for an existing topic the broker handled both commands after checking only that the client connection was authenticated unlike the broker s other topic commands such as those for creating producers and consumers or for looking up topics these two commands did not check whether the authenticated client was authorized for the target topic the pulsar rest api endpoints for schemas were not affected an authenticated client without any permission on the target topic namespace or tenant could use these commands to read the schema registered for a topic in another namespace or tenant disclosing the schema definition such as record field names and types message payloads are not disclosed register a new schema version on an existing topic in another namespace or tenant the topic s schema compatibility and schema auto update policies still apply the issue does not allow message data to be read or modified but a registered schema version can cause legitimate producers and consumers of that topic to fail with schema incompatibility errors until the schema is corrected by an administrator the standard pulsar client performs an authorized topic lookup before it sends these commands so the missing check could not be observed when testing with the standard client a client that implements the binary protocol directly is not required to perform that lookup first this issue is relevant only to deployments that have authentication and authorization enabled the getschema command is affected from apache pulsar 2 2 0 and the getorcreateschema command from apache pulsar 2 5 0 after the fix the broker requires the lookup permission on the topic for getschema and the produce permission on the topic for getorcreateschema this impact analysis assumes that pulsar has been configured with the default authorization provider for custom authorization providers the impact could be slightly different this issue affects apache pulsar versions from 2 2 0 before 4 0 14 from 4 1 0 through 4 1 3 and from 4 2 0 before 4 2 5 4 0 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 0 14 4 1 x and 4 2 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 2 5 users operating versions prior to those listed above should upgrade to the aforementioned patched versions or newer versions the currently supported apache pulsar release lines are 4 0 x and 5 0 x the supported versions schedule is available at https pulsar apache org contribute release policy

fullName: The Apache Pulsar WebSocket service allows a WebSocket consumer to configure a dead letter policy through query parameters of the consumer endpoint, including the deadLetterTopic parameter that names the topic to which messages are written
normalized: cve 2026 105927 the apache pulsar websocket service allows a websocket consumer to configure a dead letter policy through query parameters of the consumer endpoint including the deadlettertopic parameter that names the topic to which messages are written after the maximum number of redeliveries is exceeded when authorization is enabled the websocket service checks only that the connecting user holds the consume permission on the subscribed topic it does not check whether the user holds the produce permission on the topic named in deadlettertopic the dead letter messages are then written by the websocket service using its own broker client identity rather than the identity of the connecting user as a result an authenticated user who holds the consume permission on at least one topic can cause messages to be written to a topic of their choosing in any existing namespace including namespaces belonging to other tenants provided the role used by the websocket service to connect to the brokers is authorized to produce to that topic and the topic accepts a producer that registers no schema the dead letter producer created by the websocket service registers no schema so it is rejected when the target topic has a schema and schema validation is enforced for that topic or its namespace this setting is not enabled by default the same user is refused when attempting to produce to that topic directly where automatic topic creation is enabled which is the default the named topic is created if it does not already exist the issue can only be triggered when the websocket service is enabled either in the broker websocketserviceenabled which is disabled by default or as a standalone websocket proxy the impact is unauthorized injection of messages into topics the user is not permitted to produce to the user can determine the content of the injected messages when they also control the messages on the subscribed topic the issue does not allow reading modifying or deleting existing messages in the target topic injected messages carry the dead letter message properties and a dead letter producer name so they can be distinguished from messages produced normally however the values of these properties are not authenticated and should not be relied upon to establish the origin of a message whether an injected message has further consequences depends on how the applications consuming the target topic process it repeated injection also consumes storage and backlog capacity in the target namespace this issue affects apache pulsar versions from 2 3 0 before 4 0 14 and from 4 1 0 before 4 2 5 4 0 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 0 14 4 1 x and 4 2 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 2 5 users operating versions prior to those listed above should upgrade to the aforementioned patched versions or newer versions the currently supported apache pulsar release lines are 4 0 x and 5 0 x the supported versions schedule is available at https pulsar apache org contribute release policy users who cannot upgrade immediately and do not require the websocket service should disable it where the websocket service is required restricting network access to it and limiting the permissions granted to the role the websocket service uses to connect to the brokers to the namespaces websocket clients are intended to access reduces the exposure

affected versions as a result when authentication and authorization are enabled an authenticated user who has been granted produce or consume permission on a non persistent topic or on its namespace but not permission to manage the topic s policies can read replace or remove the topic level entry filter policy of that topic these operations should be restricted to users with the tenant admin role or the superuser role this impact analysis assumes that pulsar has been configured with the default authorization provider for custom authorization providers the impact could be slightly different the practical impact is limited by two broker configuration requirements neither of which is met by default entry filters must have been installed by the operator entry filter implementations are loaded only at broker startup from the broker s entry filters directory which is empty by default a request can only select among entry filters the operator has already deployed setting any other filter name is rejected the issue does not allow a caller to install or load entry filter code or to run arbitrary code in the broker topic level entry filter policies must be allowed to override the broker level configuration allowoverrideentryfilters which is disabled by default when this setting is disabled the topic level entry filter policy has no effect on message dispatch in deployments where both different installed entry filter that withholds messages from subscriptions of that topic removing it makes the topic fall back to the namespace level or broker level entry filters which are not disconnected dispatchers that already exist keep the entry filters they were created with because non persistent topics do not store messages messages withheld by an entry filter are not delivered namespace level entry filter policies are not affected apache pulsar versions before 3 3 0 are not affected because in those versions the entry filters topic policy check is made in code shared by the initialization if a step of this initialization fails for example because of an error reading from the metadata store a failure loading the topic level policies or a failure in a later initialization step the broker logs a warning disables the encryption requirement for that topic and completes the topic load as if it had succeeded the topic is then served with encryption required not enforced even though the namespace policy requires it topic level policies that could not be loaded are also not applied while the encryption requirement is not enforced an authenticated client with permission to produce to the affected topic can publish messages that are not encrypted and the broker accepts and stores them this applies both to producers created after the topic was loaded and to producers that were already connected messages published with encryption remain encrypted the issue does not expose the content of encrypted messages or the encryption keys the condition is not limited to transient failures if the cause of the initialization failure persists the encryption requirement is disabled again each time the topic is loaded for example after a topic unload a namespace bundle reassignment or a broker restart an update to the namespace policies restores enforcement on a loaded topic but only until the topic is loaded again enforcement is reliably restored only once the underlying cause of the failure has been resolved and the topic has been loaded again the broker logs a warning when the encryption requirement is disabled but the topic load is reported as successful and the state of the encryption requirement is not shown in the topic statistics in fixed versions a failure during topic initialization causes the topic load to fail so that it can be retried instead of loading the topic with the encryption requirement disabled this issue affects apache pulsar versions from 1 22 0 incubating before 4 0 14 and from 4 1 0 before 4 2 5 4 0 x version users should these paths the broker authorizes the caller only against the topic being created or updated it does not authorize the caller against the source topic named in the property the existing authorization for shadow topic configuration the shadow topic topic policy on the source topic is applied only to the source side shadow topics admin api not to these paths as a result an authenticated user who is allowed to create topics or update topic properties in one tenant can bind a topic in that tenant to a persistent topic in any other tenant with the default authorization provider these operations require the tenant admin role for the user s own tenant the user does not need any permission on the source topic its namespace or its tenant this impact analysis assumes that pulsar has been configured with the default authorization provider for custom authorization providers the impact could be different the user can then consume from the shadow topic using only permissions on their own topic and receive retained messages that were published to the source topic in the other tenant exposure is limited to messages that are still retained and readable in the source topic s ledgers messages protected with client side end to end encryption cannot be decrypted without the encryption keys a producer on the shadow topic can also register a new schema version under the source topic s schema subject to the schema compatibility settings existing schema versions are not replaced in addition the shadow topic s managed ledger applies its own retention trimming offloading and deletion to the source topic s ledgers this can permanently delete the source topic s ledger data from bookkeeper and from tiered storage regardless of the source topic s own subscriptions and retention policy including messages that have not yet been acknowledged deleting the shadow topic can also delete the source topic s ledgers this data loss can also affect shadow topics that were configured intentionally by administrators this issue affects apache pulsar versions from 3 0 0 before 4 0 14 and from 4 1 0 before 4 2 5 apache pulsar 2 x releases do not contain the shadow topic implementation 4 0 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 0 14 4 1 x and 4 2 x version users should upgrade to at least 4 2 5 users operating versions prior to those listed above should upgrade to the the role name only such as the default authorization provider are not affected by this flaw the multi role token authorization provider multirolestokenauthorizationprovider added in apache pulsar 2 8 1 resolves roles from the role claim of the token in the authentication data it is given when a proxy authenticates to the broker with its own token the original principal was therefore authorized
